content:
Rain in the bamboo and frost on the scree decide what to pack for hiking Mt Kenya. You need broken-in waterproof boots, layers that finish with a down jacket, a hooded shell, two pairs of gloves, a balaclava, a headlamp, 2-3 litres of reusable bottles and a sleeping bag rated well below freezing.

Most climbs to Point Lenana (4,985 m) take four or five days and cross four climate zones, from muddy forest near the gates to a 3:00am summit push in wind and ice. Pack too little and summit night is miserable; pack too much and your duffel goes over the porters' limit. Below: the kit list, zone by zone, what to carry and what to leave in Nairobi.

Quick Facts

  • Trekking summit: Point Lenana, 4,985 m; Batian and Nelion need technical climbing.
  • Typical trip: 4-5 days on the Sirimon, Naro Moru or Chogoria routes.
  • Coldest hours: the summit push starts around 2:00-3:00am, and summit mornings can drop to about -10°C.
  • Bag split: what to pack for hiking Mt Kenya divides between a 25-35 litre daypack and a porter duffel of about 15 kg.
  • Plastic rules: single-use plastic bottles, cups, plates, cutlery and straws are banned in Kenya's parks.
  • Driest months: January-February and roughly July-September; long rains roughly March-May, short rains roughly October-December.

What to Pack for Hiking Mt Kenya: The 25-Item Kit List

The list comes down to warmth and dryness, plus sleeping gear if your operator does not supply it.

Before buying anything, ask your operator what they provide. Many organised climbs include tents, cooking kit and meals, and some hire out sleeping bags and mats. Once you know, the table below shows what to pack for hiking Mt Kenya, and anything already supplied drops off it.

Notice there is no outfit per day. Wear the same walking clothes most of the climb and keep one dry set for camp; that alone trims what to pack for hiking Mt Kenya by a few kilos.

How Cold Does Mt Kenya Get, Zone by Zone?

Altitude shapes what to pack for hiking Mt Kenya more than anything: the mountain runs from wet forest at the gates to about -10°C on summit mornings. You add and remove the same layers as you climb rather than packing new ones.

ZoneApprox. altitudeWhat it feels likeWhat you wear
Forest and bamboo2,000-3,000 mHumid, muddy, afternoon rainBase layer, trekking trousers, shell to hand
Moorland3,000-3,800 mSunny mornings, later showersBase layer, fleece, sun hat
Alpine high campabout 4,000-4,300 mFreezing after darkThermals, fleece, down jacket, warm hat
Summit push4,300-4,985 mWind, ice, about -10°C at dawnFour upper layers, two pairs of gloves, balaclava

The Sirimon route shows the pattern. You start at Sirimon Gate (about 2,600 m), sleep at Old Moses Camp (about 3,300 m), then climb to Shipton's Camp (about 4,200 m). Our Mt Kenya hiking guide to the four main routes covers the others.

What should you wear on summit night?

Wear every warm layer at once: a base layer, a second thermal or light fleece, a thicker fleece and a down jacket, with the shell on top if the wind picks up. On the legs, thermal leggings under trekking trousers, plus over-trousers in wind.

Hands and face suffer first, so the summit-night part of what to pack for hiking Mt Kenya is liner gloves inside insulated gloves, a warm hat and a fleece-lined balaclava you can pull over your nose. Our piece on layering for cold-weather hikes explains each layer.

What Goes in Your Daypack and What Goes to the Porters?

Your daypack holds everything you might need before camp; porters carry the rest. Porters often arrive first, so expect your duffel only in the afternoon.

What to pack for hiking Mt Kenya in your daypack

Carry your shell and over-trousers, a fleece, a warm hat and gloves, 2-3 litres of water, snacks, sunscreen, sunglasses, a small first aid kit, toilet paper and your headlamp. Line the pack with a dry bag, because forest showers can be heavy during the rains.

What to pack for hiking Mt Kenya in the porter duffel

The duffel takes your sleeping bag, camp clothes, spare socks, thermals, toiletries and extra snacks. Put the sleeping bag and dry clothes in their own dry bags. Porters commonly carry up to about 20 kg, so weigh your bag in Nairobi against your operator's limit before you leave.

A common mistake is packing the down jacket in the duffel; cloud and wind reach Shipton's long before the porters do.

What Should You Not Pack for Mt Kenya?

Leave behind cotton, jeans, single-use plastic and heavy extras. Cotton stays wet and cold, and plastic water bottles are not allowed in the park.

Since 5 June 2020, single-use plastics such as water bottles, cups, disposable plates, cutlery and straws have been banned in Kenya's protected areas, including national parks and forests. The UN Environment Programme summary of the ban explains it; bring refillable bottles and dry bags instead.

Leave the laptop, a full-size towel and city shoes with your hotel or operator. Knowing what to pack for hiking Mt Kenya is half the job; resisting the just-in-case extras is the other half.

Pro Tips: Packing for Mt Kenya

  • Keep the down jacket, hat and gloves in your daypack every day.
  • At high camp, sleep with tomorrow's base layer and your water bottle inside the sleeping bag so neither freezes.
  • Print the list of what to pack for hiking Mt Kenya and tick it off as you load each bag.
  • Confirm current park fees and rules with Kenya Wildlife Service before you travel.

How Do You Get Your Kit Ready Before the Climb?

Start sorting what to pack for hiking Mt Kenya four to six weeks out. Buy or borrow the big items first, break in your boots, then test the whole system on two or three long day hikes near Nairobi.

  1. Wear new or thrifted boots on at least three long walks so pressure points show up early.
  2. Do a test hike with your daypack loaded as it will be on the mountain; Mt Longonot and the Ngong Hills are both within two hours of the city.
  3. Lay out what to pack for hiking Mt Kenya at home and drop anything unused on the test hike.
  4. Weigh the duffel and daypack against your operator's limit.

Season changes the list too. During the short rains, roughly October to December, what to pack for hiking Mt Kenya leans harder on waterproofs: a reliable shell, over-trousers and spare dry socks become non-negotiable. For muddy boots afterwards, see our boot care advice for Nairobi hikers.

Frequently Asked Questions

How many layers do I really need for Mt Kenya?

Most climbers need four upper-body layers for summit night: a base layer, a light fleece or second thermal, a thicker fleece and a down or synthetic jacket, with a shell on top in wind. On the legs, thermal leggings, trekking trousers and waterproof over-trousers are enough.

What to pack for hiking Mt Kenya if porters carry my bag?

With porters, the list splits into two bags. The duffel, usually kept near 15 kg, holds your sleeping bag, camp clothes and spares. Your 25-35 litre daypack carries waterproofs, a fleece, a warm hat, gloves, water, snacks, sun protection, first aid and a headlamp, since you may not see the duffel until the afternoon.

Is it cold at the top of Mt Kenya?

Yes. Point Lenana at 4,985 m is below freezing on summit mornings, and around -10°C is possible before wind chill. Climbers usually leave high camp at about 2:00-3:00am, the coldest hours of the day. Insulated gloves, a balaclava and a down jacket are what keep that morning safe.

What to pack for hiking Mt Kenya in the rainy season?

In the rainy season, add to the normal kit list rather than replacing it. Bring a hooded shell you trust, waterproof over-trousers, gaiters, a rain cover and dry bags, and an extra two pairs of socks. Expect muddy forest sections and a change into dry camp clothes every afternoon.

Can I buy everything for Mt Kenya in Nairobi?

Yes, you can buy everything for Mt Kenya in Nairobi, from boots and thermals to sleeping bags and headlamps. Quality thrifted gear from big outdoor brands lowers the cost of warm layers considerably. Shop a few weeks early so you can break in boots on a day hike.

Final Thoughts

A good Mt Kenya bag is mostly layers you can add or peel off in under a minute, wrapped in waterproofs and kept in dry bags. Get the boots, gloves, balaclava and sleeping bag right and the rest of what to pack for hiking Mt Kenya follows the table above.
